source.name: thinkbroadband Local Broadband Statistics (Lewisham), derived from Ofcom's postcode-level open coverage data
source.notes: 80.96% of premises in Lewisham (rounded to 81%) have full-fibre (FTTP) access as of 17 July 2026, per thinkbroadband's local broadband statistics for Lewisham (E09000023) - an independent aggregator that builds its local-authority figures from Ofcom's own postcode-level open coverage dataset rather than running its own survey. This replaces the UK-wide 82% figure previously shown here: a genuine Lewisham-specific figure is available and is preferred over the national one. Ofcom's Connected Nations data is also published as a standalone local-authority indicator on ONS's 'Explore local statistics' service ('Gigabit-capable broadband', Ofcom-sourced, January 2026 vintage), confirming this granularity is officially available, though its interactive chart doesn't expose a plain-text figure; thinkbroadband's number is used as the concrete Lewisham figure instead. No ward-level (Ladywell-specific) breakdown exists - Ofcom and its aggregators publish at local-authority and postcode level, not electoral ward - so borough-level is the most granular figure available. Gigabit-capable coverage (a broader measure that also includes Virgin Media's DOCSIS3.1 cable network) is higher, at 91.57% of Lewisham premises. No historical Lewisham-specific series exists - thinkbroadband's figure is a live snapshot, not an archive - so no trend chart is shown here; nationally, UK-wide full-fibre coverage grew from 10% of premises in 2019 to 82% by January 2026, and Lewisham's local figure sits close to that national trajectory.

source.name: Ofcom Connected Nations (Spring 2026 update), via ONS 'Explore local statistics' - 5G coverage (Lewisham)
source.notes: Lewisham's own figure is now available and replaces the England-wide 81% previously shown here: 99.8% of Lewisham's geographic area has outdoor 5G signal from at least one mobile network operator (Ofcom's -110dBm 'high confidence' threshold), per Ofcom Connected Nations data as of January 2026, published via ONS's 'Explore local statistics' local-authority indicator ('5G coverage', E09000023). This is the same metric definition (outdoor, at least one operator, % of geographic area) as the England figure it replaces, so the two remain directly comparable. This session's network policy still blocks a direct fetch of the live ONS/Ofcom pages (as it did previously, when this same borough-level breakdown was flagged as existing but unreachable), so the figure is taken from search-engine result snippets of those pages rather than a direct read of the page itself; it's independently corroborated by a third-party mobile-coverage aggregator (connection-technologies.co.uk) citing the same 99.8% figure and Spring-2026-update vintage, which is why confidence is kept at 'medium' rather than 'high'. The near-total figure fits the pattern already noted elsewhere in this entry: Lewisham is fully urban and built-up, so its whole area sits within dense coverage footprints (97-99% indoor urban 4G vs 77-85% rural, per the same Ofcom report), unlike England's landmass figure (81% in July 2025, up from 76% in 2024), which is dragged down by rural not-spots - England's national trend is kept below as context, not a genuine Lewisham time series, since no historical Lewisham-specific series was found. No ward-level (Ladywell-specific) breakdown exists - Ofcom and ONS publish at local-authority level, not electoral ward - so borough is the most granular figure available, same as the full-fibre indicator above.

target.text: No official target exists for this composite risk index - it's designed to identify relative risk, not track progress against a threshold. Lower scores indicate lower risk of digital exclusion.

source.name: Digital Exclusion Risk Index (DERI) v1.5 - Greater Manchester Combined Authority
source.notes: The GLA/LOTI 'Mapping Digital Exclusion' dataset previously cited as the intended source for this indicator is genuinely limited to its five pilot boroughs (Barnet, Brent, Kensington & Chelsea, Southwark, Westminster) - Lewisham isn't covered, and no Lewisham-specific output has been published from it, confirmed via the London Datastore and LOTI's own project pages. GMCA's Digital Exclusion Risk Index (DERI) does cover every LSOA in England, Scotland and Wales, so Ladywell's 7 constituent LSOAs (E01003273/274/275/276/278/279/291, confirmed via ONS's official LSOA-to-ward best-fit lookup) are all scored. 2.5 is the population-weighted average of those 7 LSOAs' individual DERI scores, using DERI's Great-Britain-normalised variant (England IMD basis) - the only one of DERI's three normalisation options (local authority / nation / Great Britain) that's comparable across different areas, per GMCA's own methodology guide. Scores range from 2.06 to 3.18 across the 7 LSOAs, i.e. genuine within-ward variation rather than a flat borough figure. Ladywell's score sits toward the low end of the 0-10 scale, consistent with Trust for London's own commentary that 'much of London, due to its relatively young demographic and good broadband access, is in the lower range' nationally. Caveat: DERI is a composite built from 11 proxy indicators (deprivation, demography, broadband access) across three domains, not a direct survey of who's actually offline, and several of its components are dated - 'no qualifications', 'social grade' and 'day-to-day activities limited' all come from Census 2011, while IMD is 2019-based and broadband/unemployment/pension-credit data is from 2019-2021. GMCA's in-progress v2.0 rebuild moves to 2021 Census data but has not yet published a scored output, so v1.5 remains the latest version with a usable score. The previous indicator here - GLA's 2022 estimate of ~270,000 Londoners completely offline (London-wide, not Lewisham-specific) - is kept as descriptive context below rather than as the snapshot, since it measures something DERI doesn't (an absolute headcount rather than a relative risk score).

source.name: TfL Public Transport Accessibility Levels (PTAL) / WebCAT - GIS Open Data Hub
source.notes: TfL does not publish a single official 'ward average' PTAL figure - PTAL is a point-by-point accessibility calculation (walk time and service frequency to the nearest public transport stops), surfaced via TfL's WebCAT tool and this GIS layer, not aggregated to ward or borough geography. Genuine point-level PTAL values within Ladywell were instead sourced from real Lewisham Council planning application assessments, which cite TfL's PTAL methodology directly: 31 Gillian Street (application DC/25/139782, Sept 2025, https://lewisham.moderngov.co.uk/mgAi.aspx?ID=37128) was assessed at PTAL 4 ('good'), while the Ladywell Playtower site on Ladywell Road, immediately by Ladywell station (application DC/22/126038, https://lewisham.moderngov.co.uk/mgAi.aspx?ID=32690), was assessed at PTAL 6 ('excellent'). Lewisham's own Local Plan evidence base describes the borough's northern, western and central neighbourhoods - which include Ladywell, served directly by Ladywell mainline station - as its best-connected, with southern wards less well served. TfL refreshed its PTAL toolkit to 'WebCAT 3.0' in 2025, updating scores from a 2015 baseline (with an interim 2019 borough-level PDF release for Lewisham) to reflect network changes since, including the Elizabeth line. No numeric trend is included: PTAL is a periodic recalculation exercise tied to toolkit versions (2015, 2019, 2025), not an annual survey, and no single ward-wide figure exists to trend consistently across those versions.

source.notes: Underlying source: TfL's London Travel Demand Survey (LTDS), a continuous household survey of ~8,000 households/year. The most recent Healthy Streets Scorecard (2026, reported July 2026 by Salamander News, a Lewisham community news site) put mode share at approximately 72%, a further ~1-point fall, with Lewisham last in Inner London for the third year running. Caution: the Scorecard's methodology changed between rounds - the 2024 figure used a single year of LTDS data, while the 2025 round moved to a two-year rolling average (2022/23-2023/24) - so year-to-year movements should be read with that in mind, per the Scorecard's own published small-sample-size caveat for borough-level LTDS estimates.

source.name: MHCLG English Indices of Deprivation 2025, aggregated to Ladywell ward
source.notes: Ward-level aggregation (per DIMENSION_PAGE_SPECIFICATION.md 1.6/11.6): Ladywell ward comprises 7 LSOAs (Lower-layer Super Output Areas, ~1,000-3,000 people each); 1 of the 7 (about 14%) ranks in England's most deprived national quintile (IMD decile 1-2), per Lewisham Observatory's Ladywell ward profile (observatory.lewisham.gov.uk/ladywell/) and corroborated by Ladywell Live's report on the IMD 2025 release (31 Oct 2025), which also states Ladywell's position 'has changed little since 2019' and that the ward scores comparatively well on the education domain specifically but poorly on income and living environment - directly relevant to this dimension. Full LSOA-by-LSOA decile aggregation (rather than this single 'how many of 7 are in the bottom quintile' statistic) was not feasible this session because the underlying LSOA-level dataset could not be downloaded (WebFetch blocked site-wide - see function docstring); this is a genuine, sourced ward aggregation rather than the borough-average fallback. Borough context: Lewisham LA ranks 172nd-least-deprived of 296 English local authorities on IMD 2025's 'Rank of Extent' summary measure (only 2% of Lewisham's LSOAs sit in the nationally most-deprived decile, vs 10% for England as a whole) - but this is a narrower, different summary measure from the LA's overall/average-rank deprivation position, which has historically been far more deprived-looking (48th of 326 local authorities under IMD 2015's average-rank measure; PHE's 2019 health profile classed Lewisham as 'one of the 20% most deprived districts/unitary authorities in England'). These different summary measures are NOT combined into one trend - IMD is not designed for cross-round comparison in any case (MHCLG's own IMD 2025 guidance cautions against directly comparing ranks/deciles across releases, since both the indicator set and LSOA boundaries change between rounds), so a single 2025 data point is used rather than a fabricated series.
